title: More stopovers facilitate migratory waterfowl tracking shifting vegetation green‐up
content:
By integrating tracking data from multiple migratory waterfowl species with remote sensing data, we showed that birds using more stopover sites are better able to synchronize their schedules with vegetation green-up at their breeding grounds. Our findings highlight the importance of stopover sites in enhancing birds' resilience to climate change.


Abstract

Climate change is altering the phenology of food resources, and migratory birds may respond by adjusting migration timing to track shifting food availability (i.e. their phenological sensitivity). The ability to adjust migration timing can vary among species according to traits such as ecological guild, body size and migration distance. Stopover sites are critical components of migration, allowing birds to refuel and acquire updated environmental information. However, empirical evidence on how stopover use enhances phenological sensitivity to shifting spring green-up remains lacking. In this study, we investigated how stopover frequency influences the phenological sensitivity of migratory waterfowl at breeding areas. We hypothesized that individuals using more stopover sites would better align their migration timing with shifts in vegetation green-up. We reconstructed 220 spring migration paths from five East Asian migratory waterfowl species using high-resolution tracking data collected from 2015 to 2023. Spring vegetation green-up was derived from remote sensing data. We then fitted linear mixed models to test how stopover frequency influences the change of arrival timing at breeding sites. Individuals using a greater number of stopover sites showed closer alignment between their migration timing and local spring vegetation green-up at breeding areas. More frequent stopover use was associated with stronger phenological sensitivity, suggesting greater behavioural plasticity in tracking shifting resources. Loss of stopover habitat may therefore limit their capacity to respond to changing resource phenology, underscoring the importance of stopover conservation for promoting resilience to climate change.

中文摘要

气候变化正在改变食物资源的物候，迁徙鸟类可能通过调整迁徙时间来追踪不断变化的食物可利用性，即表现出对资源物候变化的物候敏感性。不同物种调整迁徙时间的能力可能因生态类群、体型和迁徙距离等性状而异。停歇地是迁徙过程中的关键组成部分，不仅为鸟类提供补充能量的场所，也有助于其获取最新的环境信息。然而，关于停歇地利用如何影响迁徙鸟类对春季植被返青变化的物候敏感性，目前仍缺乏实证证据。 本研究探讨了停歇地利用频率如何影响迁徙水鸟在繁殖地的物候敏感性。我们假设，利用更多停歇地的个体能够更好地调整迁徙时间，从而使到达繁殖地的时间与春季植被返青变化保持更紧密的同步。 基于2015-2023年高分辨率追踪数据，我们重建了5种东亚迁徙水鸟共220条春季迁徙路线，并利用遥感数据获取春季植被返青时间。随后，我们构建线性混合效应模型，检验停歇地利用频率对繁殖地到达时间变化的影响。 结果表明，利用更多中途停歇地的个体，其迁徙时间与繁殖地当地春季植被返青变化之间表现出更高程度的匹配。中途停歇地利用数量越多，个体表现出的物候敏感性越强，表明更频繁地利用中途停歇地可能有助于迁徙水鸟通过行为可塑性追踪不断变化的资源物候。因此，中途停歇地栖息地的丧失可能限制迁徙水鸟应对资源物候变化的能力。这一发现凸显了保护迁徙停歇地对于增强其应对气候变化能力的重要性。
